newsitem.title: USA: Southwest hit by fears of "user fee" plan.
newsitem.headline: Southwest hit by fears of "user fee" plan.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co's stock price dropped Monday after a government report warned that smaller airlines would be hurt by a "user-fee" plan proposed by seven major carriers, analysts said.
Major airlines, including UAL Corp, AMR Corp and Continental Airlines Inc, proposed a "user fee plan" as an alternative to the current 10 percent excise tax on every ticket.
The excise tax, which helps to fund the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration, will expire Dec. 31.
The GAO report suggested that the proposed user-fee plan would favor larger airlines at the expense of smaller, low-cost carriers.

"If it (user-fee plan) went through, it would raise taxes on short-haul providers," said Steve Lewins, an airline analyst with Gruntal & Co. "It's good for long-haul, first class carriers, but it is not economically sound," Lewins said.
Lewins estimates that the user-fee plan would increase the cost of air travel on small, regional carriers. That increase would stop about 26 million passengers a year from traveling.
Southwest's stock dropped 1/2 to 24-1/4 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Southwest's stock felt additional pressure due to its dim fourth quarter outlook.
As Southwest previously warned, it expects its fourth quarter earnings to be "substantially below" last year's levels.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, Southwest earned $43 million or $0.29 a share.

During the current fourth quarter, revenue per available seat mile fell due to strong demand for leisure fares as well as increased trip lengths, Southwest chief executive officer Herbert Kelleher said in a statement.
"Based on these trends and significantly higher jet fuel prices, our fourth quarter 1996 earnings will be substantially below last year's record fourth quarter earnings," Kelleher said.
